clue.text: Spooner's chief betrayer finds status symbol in church

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of two neighbouring words

parts.note: the chief of an organisation is its head
a rat is someone who informs on or deserts his friends

explanation.surface: A clumsy-tongued clergyman's leading traitor comes across a mark of rank inside a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' swaps the opening sounds of HEAD RAT, and the result is respelt. The headgear is the scarlet one a Catholic cardinal receives.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-style description: a cardinal's scarlet headgear marks his high rank in the Catholic hierarchy.

clue.text: Victory, perhaps, and flowers with it

parts.note: flags are irises, a kind of flower
with it and hip both mean fashionably up to date

explanation.surface: A triumph, maybe, and the bouquets that come along with winning.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Victory was Nelson's vessel at Trafalgar, leading the British fleet; the capital letter hides in plain sight at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: HMS Victory carried Admiral Nelson at Trafalgar and so led the fleet.

clue.text: VAT, maximum, for knitwear?

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquid
the top speed or price is the maximum one

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether sales tax is charged at the highest rate on woollens.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's sales tax, printed in capitals to disguise an ordinary container. In Britain the garment is a sleeveless knitted pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in British usage this is a sleeveless knitted pullover worn over a shirt.

clue.text: Return of a pothole in road shortly to be expected?

indicators.note: a return sends the whole assembled run back the way it came, right to left
in places the article and the pothole inside the shortened road
shortly cuts the road word short by its final letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
a rut is a hole or groove worn in a road surface

explanation.surface: A hole in the highway that was mended is soon likely to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the road, 'in' fills it to make LARUTAN, and 'Return of' turns that whole run round. The surface is a motorist's weary complaint about roadworks that never last.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outcome that is only normal is one anybody would have predicted.

clue.text: Little fish here, skinned?

parts.note: fry are newly hatched young fish

indicators.note: skinned strips the outside letters from the word, as skin is the outer layer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the tiddlers in this spot have had their skins removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' takes the outside letters off 'here'. The whole clue also describes the pan in a chip shop where small fish, often skinned, end up.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole-clue description: small fish, perhaps with skins removed, are cooked in such a pan of hot oil.

clue.text: Behaving badly, having no breeding

definitions.meaning: said of someone overstepping the limits of acceptable conduct
read literally, lacking a pedigree or lineage of ancestors

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom plus whimsical literal reading: overstepping acceptable conduct, and lacking any ancestry or pedigree.

clue.text: Where honest cops are based? Well…

definitions.meaning: nick is British slang for a police station, so virtuous officers would work at a virtuous one

explanation.definitionFit: Punning description of a virtuous police station, and a British idiom for being healthy or in sound condition.

clue.text: Dye originally worn as decoration, hiding nothing

indicators.note: hiding means the initials conceal the extra letter among themselves
originally points to the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pigment first used as body ornament, leaving nothing uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the initials W, A, D and 'hiding' puts O inside them. Ancient Britons are said to have painted themselves blue with this plant pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a blue colouring made from a plant, used by ancient Britons as body paint.

clue.text: Large within and without, turning smooth

indicators.note: turning sends the assembled letters round to read from right to left
one sense of large goes inside while another sense sits outside it

parts.note: large means big
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Something roomy both inside and outside becomes sleek as it rotates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' works twice: L 'within' and BIG 'without', giving BLIG, which 'turning' sends backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a smooth talker is fluent and plausible, perhaps insincerely so.

clue.text: Harsh adjustment to net ratings

indicators.note: an adjustment to something alters it, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A severe revision is made to a broadcaster's overall viewing figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: severe or biting, as of criticism or a sharp taste.

clue.text: Hand out drink during piano playing

indicators.note: during places the drink in the middle of the rearranged instrument
playing suggests the letters of the instrument are in motion and rearranged

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone serves refreshments while the pianist performs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' is not a performance: it rearranges the instrument's letters to APION, and 'during' places the drink in the middle of that.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to share something among people, giving each a part.

clue.text: Queen put on hat to dance

indicators.note: put on says the monarch's letters are added to the end of the headgear

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: The monarch dons her headgear ready for a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' attaches ER, the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II, to CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to skip or frolic about in a lively way.

clue.text: Doubt expressed about cutting unusual April flower

indicators.note: cutting means the hesitation slices into the rearranged month
unusual says the month's letters are not in their normal order
about turns the hesitation round to read the other way

parts.note: um is the sound made when hesitating or doubtful

explanation.surface: Someone voices misgivings about snipping a rare spring bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the month to PRILA, 'about' turns the hesitation backwards, and 'cutting' slots it inside. 'Doubt expressed' is a spoken noise, not a stated opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the genus of plants that includes the primrose and cowslip, blooming in spring.

clue.text: Famous London statue with one leg wearing away

parts.note: Eros is the popular name of the winged figure on the fountain in Piccadilly Circus, London
I is the Roman numeral for one
in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A well-known monument in the capital has a single limb crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros stands in Piccadilly Circus in London; 'leg' is the cricket term for the on side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: the gradual grinding down of rock or stone by weather.

clue.text: Source of jelly coating good part of mechanism

indicators.note: coating means the jelly source forms a layer round the outside of the other letter

parts.note: cow heel, the foot of an ox, is stewed to make jelly

explanation.surface: Something that yields gelatine is smeared over a sound piece of machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' wraps COWHEEL round G. Cow heel is the foot of an ox, a traditional British dish stewed to a jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a toothed disc that meshes with others inside a machine or clock.

clue.text: Run to end of arena following car

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that comes next

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Someone sprints to the far side of a stadium behind a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run to' looks like movement but is an idiom: if your money will run to something, you have enough for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: if funds run to a purchase, there is enough money to pay for it.

clue.text: Producing rewards without first consenting to

indicators.note: without first means the opening letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: something gratifying is rewarding, giving satisfaction

explanation.surface: Handing out prizes before anyone has agreed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without first' drops the opening G from GRATIFYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: formally approving a treaty or agreement so that it takes effect.

clue.text: Very small diamonds showing dark stain

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
fingers marked with dark blots from a pen are inky

explanation.surface: Tiny gems reveal a murky blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal synonym: attractively tiny and neat.

clue.text: Queen seized by hostile troops at the front

indicators.note: seized by means the monarch is grabbed and held inside the word for hostile

parts.note: to be anti something is to be hostile or opposed to it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth II
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: The monarch is captured by enemy soldiers in the battle line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seized by' puts the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II inside the word for hostile. 'troops' is the British Army's 'other ranks', soldiers below officer level.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: situated forward or before, the opposite of posterior.

clue.text: Extremists in cult fearing upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Zealots inside a sect are distressed by their dread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder that 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the wildest and most fanatical members on the edge of a movement.

clue.text: Start to sleep in shed

definitions.meaning: to begin sleeping, to drop into slumber
to remove something, such as a garment, from oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Two idiomatic phrasal-verb senses: to drop into slumber, and to remove something such as clothing.

clue.text: Lion about to catch buck in Veldt, initially no meat-eater

indicators.note: to catch means the hero and his neighbour take hold of the initials inside them

parts.note: a lion is a brave or celebrated person, a hero

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A big cat on the African grassland is about to seize a deer, having never before eaten flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the opening letters of three words, not one, and 'to catch' places them inside the two joined pieces. 'Lion' is a celebrated person, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an animal that feeds only on plants and never on flesh.

clue.text: Pound of beans?

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to throb or beat strongly, as a heart does
beans, peas and lentils are edible seeds of this class

explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to throb, and the food class covering edible seeds like lentils and peas.

clue.text: Go on claiming old heretic's divine

indicators.note: claiming means the chatter takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: to go on is to talk at tedious length, to prate
a Gnostic belonged to an early sect the Church condemned as heretical

explanation.surface: Keep asserting that a long-dead dissenter was holy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claiming' wraps the word for talking at length round the other two pieces. 'divine' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to foretell or predict what will happen.

clue.text: Spotting extremely genial rogue with pipe

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: an imp is a little rascal or rogue
to pipe is to sing in a high voice, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a very friendly rascal smoking his briar.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: catching a brief sight of something.

clue.text: Reporter's brought down boring document removed from office

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the heard word goes inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a wrestler brought down by an opponent is thrown

explanation.surface: A journalist's tedious paper, since demolished, is taken away from the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reporter's' turns THROWN into its sound-alike THRON, which 'boring' drills into DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deposed, as a monarch stripped of power.

clue.text: Butcher to call it a day

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to kill; the slang phrase means to murder
to stop work when the shift is over

explanation.definitionFit: Two slang senses of one phrasal verb: to kill someone, and to finish work for the day.

clue.text: Watering facility finished with only one horse

indicators.note: with only one says that of the two copies of the horse letter just one is kept

parts.note: to be through with something is to be finished with it
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: The drinking station ended up serving a single pony.
explanation.walkthrough: THROUGH has two Hs; 'with only one' removes the first. H and 'horse' are both slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long open container from which farm animals drink.

clue.text: Setter commonly keeps visual record

indicators.note: commonly suggests common speech that drops the opening aitch of a word

parts.note: someone who keeps a thing has it
a pic is a photograph, a record you can see

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler habitually holds on to a photo archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' drops the H from HAS, as in Cockney speech. 'Setter' is not the compiler here but something that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a savoury jelly that sets firm round meat or fish.

clue.text: Player having edge in work tipped

indicators.note: in places the edge inside the upturned work
tipped means tipped over, so in a down clue the work reads upwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
the rim of a cup is its edge

explanation.surface: A sportsman with an advantage at work gets a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' is no gratuity: it upends the musical work to read PO, and 'in' puts the edge inside. The solution is the pianist taking the upper part in a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the performer of the upper part in a piano duet.
